relevance_note: One of 24 children with primary immunodeficiency in this single-centre series (Patient #18) is described individually with a TNFAIP3 variant: "Genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous c.259C>T mutation in TNFAIP3, indicating an A20 deficiency."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Scope: the cohort has 24 PID patients (cohort_size_as_stated = 24); only Patient #18 has a TNFAIP3 variant or A20 deficiency, so only Patient #18 gets rows. No relatives of Patient #18 are described. Label 'Patient #18' is the paper's text form (Table 2 prints '#18' in the 'Patient no.' column). Table 2 has patients as rows; spans quote from '| #18 |' through the cell. Table 2 'A/S' = age at diagnosis in months / sex per the legend, so 192 is recorded as age at diagnosis (P192M), not onset or last evaluation. Table 2 'Physical findings' and 'Additional manifestations' cells for #18 are '-'; the legend does not define '-', so nothing is excluded from them (rule 6). 'ND' in Table 2 is defined as 'not done'. No feature is marked excluded. 'without plasma cells' is a histopathological qualifier; its scope in 'LNH, ileitis and colitis without plasma cells' is ambiguous, so it is kept as detail, not as a separate feature. Lymphonodular hyperplasia (intestinal histology) was not mapped to the checklist item 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' (left not reported). Group-level counts (Tables 1 and 4, e.g. consanguinity 6/23 families, hypogammaglobulinemia 12/24) were not applied to Patient #18. is_proband left null: the paper does not call anyone proband and this is a series, not a single-patient case report. No protein change, transcript, inheritance, parental testing or functional data are printed for the TNFAIP3 variant. pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors records the authors' causal wording ('mutation ... indicating an A20 deficiency'); no formal class is given. Contradictions noticed elsewhere in the paper (not affecting Patient #18): Table 2 repeats the #9 row; Table 3 row #23 says 'Sibling of patient #23'; Patient #12 is said to have non-diagnostic WES in Results and Table 2 but 'Whole exome sequencing was not performed' in the Discussion.
